title: Safe draft state and human approval/resume

sources.supports: Checkpointer plus same thread ID, Command resume, default invoke __interrupt__, and replay-safe node boundaries.
ToolRuntime.state is injected and hidden from model schema; Command updates require a matching ToolMessage.
Thread-scoped checkpointers versus cross-thread stores; InMemorySaver is not restart-durable.
L10 source-context entry at 02:28:46 only; U2 is added material, not source-video code.

limitations: No live Anthropic or tracing calls were made by the lesson author; parent must validate both real run_demo entrypoints and capture execution evidence.
InMemorySaver retains pending approvals only within this process; restart durability belongs to U1's durable-backend discussion.
CLI run_demo uses explicitly scripted approve/reject responses as a reproducible demonstration, not evidence that an independent person reviewed the content.
Thread IDs separate checkpoints but do not implement authentication or authorization. The output directory must be trusted and not concurrently mutated by an attacker.

Exclusive creation prevents overwrite, but checkpoint commits and filesystem writes are not one atomic transaction. A crash or partial I/O failure needs reconciliation; exactly-once delivery is not claimed.
The workbook has one repair opportunity, not an unbounded retry loop, revision editor, GUI, or production approval service.
Use explicit rejection payloads rather than Command(resume=None); the installed LangGraph version raises internally for an empty resume command.
Only focused macOS offline tests are executed here; no Windows or production durability claims are made.
